paragraph: Ramsey's single-family market carried 40 sales over six months at a median of $999,500, essentially right at the million mark, with a sale-to-list ratio of 1.018, 55 percent of homes selling above asking, and a median of 15 days on market. That is competitive, and well-priced homes are moving fast, though sellers are not getting the across-the-board premiums you see in a full frenzy. The range runs from $470,000 to $2,450,000, so the median is the better guide than the extremes. Condos and townhouses are the tighter tier, 23 sales at a median of $605,000, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.039, roughly 65 percent selling above asking, and a median of 12 days on market. That is a real seller's market, and buyers at that price point should expect multiple offer situations. On seasonality, single-family volume built steadily through spring into summer, and July was both the heaviest month at 12 closings and one of the strongest medians at $1,250,500, so Ramsey is showing no sign yet of the usual late-summer drift. The condo months are too thin individually to read a trend from, so use the six-month picture there. If you're weighing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat, since both are tight. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance lifestyle of a townhouse or condo.
